# Architecture — what each package is, and what may depend on what

*Written 2026-09-14. The dependency graph in §2 was generated by reading every
`package.json` in the workspace, not drawn by hand. Every package's one-line job
in §3 is quoted from its own `index.ts` header.*

Companions: [`RETRIEVAL.md`](RETRIEVAL.md) · [`AUGMENTED-GENERATION.md`](AUGMENTED-GENERATION.md)
· [`ENGINES.md`](ENGINES.md) are the three deep-dives on the AI path.
[`REFACTOR-PLAN.md`](plans/REFACTOR.md) is the measurement that decided what
became a package and what deliberately did not.

> **This document charts the LOGICAL architecture — package names, contracts and
> dependency edges. It deliberately does not chart directory layout**, which is
> being restructured as this is written. See §7.

---

## The one rule

> **Buy the transport. Write the judgment.**

Everything below follows from it. Transport is the part that would look the same
at any customer: loading documents, calling a model, running evals, counting
tokens. Judgment is the part that cannot transfer: what a policy form *is*, which
failures are dangerous, what a good answer looks like. Transport is a package;
judgment is not.

The test that keeps it honest is mechanical: `pnpm leak:check` scans every
executable line of the shared packages and **fails the build if domain vocabulary
appears in one.**

---

## 1 · Three layers, and which way dependencies point

```
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  SURFACE            what a human looks at                        │
   │    four apps  +  @fde/uikit  +  @veresk/surface                  │
   └────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                │ depends on
   ┌────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  JUDGMENT           one per engagement — CANNOT transfer          │
   │    @claims/insurance · @meridian/pharma · @vantis/steering        │
   │    the corpus, the prompt, the tools, the schema, the eval cases, │
   │    the severity rules                                             │
   └────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                │ depends on
   ┌────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  TRANSPORT          domain-neutral — lifts into any customer      │
   │    grounding · agent · evals · schema · telemetry · guard ·       │
   │    scanner · estate · foundry · bedrock                           │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

   Dependencies point DOWN only. No @fde/* package imports an engagement,
   and `leak:check` fails the build if one so much as says "policy".
```

**Judgment is the big layer, and that is the finding, not an accident.**

```
  transport (10 @fde/* packages)          11,560
  judgment  (3 engagements)               41,103   ← 3.56× the shared machinery
  surface   (4 apps + uikit + surface)    30,123
```

If a "framework" ever grows larger than the judgment it serves, the split was
drawn in the wrong place.

**THESE THREE NUMBERS ARE GENERATED, AND THE PREVIOUS SET WAS NOT.** They are
the sum of `lines` in
[`architecture.generated.ts`](../apps/web/veresk-app/src/lib/learn/architecture.generated.ts),
produced by `pnpm arch:graph` from every `package.json`; `pnpm arch:check` fails
a build when the file and the manifests disagree. Regenerate rather than edit.

The set they replaced — 10,733 / 39,590 / 24,073, and a 3.7× ratio — was hand
counted, true when written, and wrong by 827, 1,513 and **6,050** lines by the
time anyone looked. The surface figure drifted worst because the `/learn`
section was added to `veresk-app` and nothing here knew. **A number in a
document that describes a repo goes stale the moment somebody works on the
repo**, which is the argument for this paragraph existing rather than for
somebody being more careful. The layer *counts* — 10, 3, 6 — did not move, and
the headline did not either: judgment is still over three times the shared
machinery.

Note on method, because the two available answers differ: a package's lines are
summed per file, so a file not ending in a newline still contributes its last
line. `cat **/*.ts | wc -l` reports one fewer per file — 92 against 94 for
`@fde/foundry`, 567 against 571 for `@fde/bedrock`. §2's diagram below uses the
older convention.

## 2 · The dependency graph, as it actually is

Generated from `package.json`, not remembered:

```
                        @fde/foundry (92)  ◄─── azure creds, short-lived
                              ▲
                              │
    ┌──────────┬──────────┬───┴──────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
    │          │          │          │          │          │          │
 @fde/     @fde/      @fde/      @fde/      @fde/      @fde/      @fde/
 agent    grounding   evals     schema   telemetry   scanner    estate
 (3481)    (2792)    (2072)     (302)      (536)      (296)      (403)
    │          │          │          │          │          │          │
    └──────────┴─────┬────┴──────────┴────┬─────┴────┬─────┴──────────┘
                     │                    │          │
         ┌───────────┼────────────┐       │          │
         │           │            │       │          │
   @claims/    @meridian/    @vantis/     │          │
   insurance     pharma      steering ────┴──────────┘
    (2,964)     (16,545)     (20,081)          ▲
         │           │            │            └── @fde/bedrock (567)
         │           │            │                 steering only
         ▼           ▼            ▼
   insurance-    pharma-app   steering-app          @fde/guard (192)
     app         (10,627)      (8,813)              insurance + the two apps
   (1,140)          │             │
         │          └──────┬──────┘
         │                 ▼
         │          @veresk/surface (613) ──► @fde/uikit (2,085)
         │                                          ▲
         └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    @veresk/app (795) ──► both
```

**Every `@fde/*` package has at least one consumer** — checked, not assumed.
Three edges are worth reading twice:

| Edge | Why it is like that |
|---|---|
| `@fde/agent` → `@fde/foundry` | the only dependency *between* transport packages other than `surface → uikit`. The loop needs a credential; it does not need a domain. |
| `@fde/bedrock` ← steering **only** | the AWS adapter exists to test the claim that *"a customer on AWS writes a sibling of `@fde/foundry` and changes nothing else."* One consumer is honest — it has one job. |
| `@fde/scanner` ← pharma **only** | new. The other two callers (`leak-check.mjs`, steering's guard) have not been converted yet — see §5. |

One genuine asymmetry, flagged rather than smoothed: **`@fde/guard` has four
consumers, and insurance is two of them.**

```
  @claims/insurance        the package — pulls it to run its self-test
  @claims/insurance-app    the app     — guarding an HTTP route
  @meridian/pharma-app     the app
  @vantis/steering-app     the app
```

Insurance consumes it *both* ways; the other two engagements only at the app,
where it belongs. Same package, two different reasons, and the shape of the
graph does not say which is which.

*Corrected 2026-09-15. This paragraph previously read "consumed by
`@claims/insurance` but by pharma's and steering's apps", which omitted
`@claims/insurance-app` and so described a cleaner split than exists. Found by
diffing this section against the generated graph — the asymmetry is real, it
was just not the one written down.*

## 4 · Inside `@fde/agent` — three engines with one shape

The largest transport package, and the one with internal structure worth a chart:

```
  core/                            SHARED BY ALL THREE — this is the contract
    loop.types.ts     LoopOptions · TurnRecord · LoopResult · DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS
    registry.ts       dispatch a tool call, shape its errors, record it
    settle.ts         when is the loop done · the ONE copy of the retry sentence
    fixtures.ts       record / replay tool calls
    tool.types.ts · usage.ts · summarise.ts · fanout.ts

  sdk/        mastra/        langgraph/      ← structurally IDENTICAL, on purpose
    provider.ts   which client, which cloud, which credential
    tools.ts      our Tool[] → this framework's tool objects
    turns.ts      this framework's reply shape → our TurnRecord
    loop.ts       the ~150 lines that actually drive it
```

Two deliberate design facts:

**The four-file split is so an engine diff is a file-vs-file read.** Before it,
each engine was one 320–364-line file and comparing two meant comparing two
essays.

**`core/settle.ts` was extracted for a correctness reason, not tidiness.** The
schema-retry *sentence* — which is a prompt — was written out three times. Three
copies means one can be reworded by a find-and-replace that misses a file, and
from then on an engine comparison silently measures a prompt difference **while
reporting it as an engine difference**. `eval:diff` would never catch it, because
the engine is part of the setup key.

What stays per-engine on purpose: `turns.ts`, because three frameworks genuinely
return three different reply shapes, and pretending otherwise is how you get an
abstraction nobody can read.

## 5 · The two newest packages, and why each earned it

Both landed 2026-09-14. Neither was proposed for being duplicated — each had a
defect behind it.

### `@fde/scanner` — three comment-strippers that disagreed

Three independent checks each walked a source tree, stripped comments, and
matched forbidden patterns: `scripts/leak-check.mjs`, pharma's write guard, and
steering's. **They disagreed, and the disagreement was a live blind spot:**
pharma's stripper cut at the first `//`, so it could not see a database write on
any line that also held a URL. `leak-check.mjs` had already suffered the same
bug class from the other side — it once passed clean while silently stripping a
real leaked credential URL, mistaking `postgresql://…` for a trailing comment.

> **One bug class, three copies, and fixing it in one says nothing about the
> others.** That is a correctness argument for a package. "These files look
> similar" is not.

### `@fde/estate` — the one measured skeleton

`db/init/{create,drop,migrate}.ts` were **53–67 % identical** between pharma and
steering — the genuine shared skeleton. One behaviour change came with the
extraction: `dropDatabases` now checks **every** name before dropping **any**.

### The boundary rule both follow

```
  SHARED      the machinery: walk, strip, match, plant · create, drop, migrate
  CALLER'S    the RULE and the DESCRIPTOR: which patterns are forbidden,
              which paths are exempt, which databases exist
  RETURNED    every function returns WHAT IT DID rather than printing it
```

That last line is the subtle one. The two callers format their output completely
differently — and formatting was the only thing they did *not* have in common. A
package that printed would have had to take a formatter parameter per caller.

It is the same split `@fde/grounding` already made: the loader is shared, the
`DocumentDomain` descriptor is passed in.

## 6 · What was deliberately NOT shared — and the measurement that decided it

The brief was *"extract everything which can be generic."* **The measurement said
most of it isn't.**

Of 16 identically-named file pairs across pharma and steering, a line-level diff
found:

```
   5 pairs   46–67 % identical   → a real skeleton   → @fde/estate
  11 pairs    3–37 % identical   → different work under the same filename
```

The 11, worst first:

```
  db/init/check.ts                3%     eval/severity/severity-selftest.ts   6%
  eval/checks/checks-selftest.ts  7%     guard/sql-write-selftest.ts          8%
  eval/run.ts                    11%     db/schema/rows.ts                   17%
  config/connections.ts          25%     tools/utils/handle.ts               25%
  grounding/embeddings.factory   37%     telemetry/prices.ts                 37%
  db/seed/world-check.ts         37%
```

`db/schema/rows.ts` is 638 lines of pharma's world and 468 of steering's. **They
are supposed to differ — that is the domain.** Sharing them would mean one file
that knows about both drug batches and steering bids, which is precisely what
`leak:check` exists to prevent.

> **Extracting the 11 would produce a shared abstraction over things that are not
> the same** — the failure mode where a package grows a parameter per caller and
> nobody can read any of it.

### Three claims that were wrong, and how

The refactor's own author records three findings that did not survive contact
with the files, all from **grepping instead of reading**:

| Claim | Reality |
|---|---|
| `@fde/guard` is duplicated by the engagements' `guard/` folders | It is an HTTP key guard; theirs are **source scanners** — a different concern. Both files already opened with a paragraph saying so. |
| steering lacks comment-stripping | It has it, deliberately and documented. |
| pharma does not use `@fde/evals` | It does, and always did — a grep matched only single-line imports and missed a multi-line one. |

> **A convergence already done looks exactly like one that is missing, if you
> measure with the wrong instrument.** The measurement in §6 held up; the
> impressions did not.

## 7 · The physical layout — three globs, and the split is the point

Landed 2026-09-14 in `8ff105a`. `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is the authority:

```
  apps/web/*          a DEPLOYABLE SURFACE
                      TanStack Start · a vite.config.ts · a port ·
                      an entry in .github/workflows/deploy.yml
      insurance-app        3000        pharma-app      3301
      steering-app         3400        veresk-app      3300

  apps/ai/*           AN ENGAGEMENT'S OWN JUDGEMENT, and its CLIs
                      agent loops · tools · prompts · schemas · evals
                      NO PORT. Imported BY the surface next door.
      insurance            pharma          steering

  packages/*          WHAT TRANSFERS
                      every @fde/*, plus @veresk/surface
      grounding  agent  evals  schema  telemetry  guard
      scanner    estate foundry bedrock uikit      surface
```

**Why the engagements moved out of `packages/`.** They were never packages in the
sense the others are — nothing installs them as a library, and they cannot
transfer by construction. Sitting them in `packages/` implied a reusability they
do not have. `apps/ai/*` says what they are: an application's brain, with no
surface of its own.

**`leak:check` did not change, and that is the load-bearing detail.** It keys on
the `@fde/` **prefix**, not on a directory — so moving the engagements out of
`packages/` did not alter what it guards. A rule anchored to a naming convention
survives a reorganisation; one anchored to a path would have silently stopped
checking.

### What a move like this actually breaks

Nothing in §1–§6 changed — names, contracts and edges are invariant under a move.
What breaks is **anything that encoded the old depth**, and two classes did:

| | |
|---|---|
| `REPO_ROOT` constants that counted `..` segments | now walk **up** looking for `pnpm-workspace.yaml` |
| `package.json` scripts with relative `../guard`, `../telemetry` paths | repointed |

> **A constant that counts directory levels is a dependency on the layout that no
> typecheck can see.** Both classes compiled perfectly before and after; only
> running them showed the difference.

Two things the move left behind, recorded rather than smoothed:

- **`pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s own header comment is stale.** It still describes
  `packages/insurance` and `apps/insurance-app`, which no longer exist. The
  `packages:` globs at the bottom are correct; the prose above them predates the
  move.
- **`insurance-app` does not boot**, and it is **not** a consequence of this move:
  it imports `@claims/insurance/security`, whose exports map points at
  `dist/security/guard.js`, and `src/security/` has never existed on any ref in
  git history. The other three surfaces serve HTTP 200.

## 8 · What holds the architecture up

```bash
pnpm leak:check        # no domain vocabulary in any @fde/* package — THE rule, enforced
pnpm typecheck         # every package
pnpm build             # every package
```

`leak:check` is the one to understand. It scans every executable line of the
shared packages and fails on insurance vocabulary. **Comments are exempt on
purpose** — the reasoning in those packages is often *about* the domain boundary,
and a package explaining why it does not know what a policy is would otherwise
fail for saying "policy".

It also **plants a synthetic leak and asserts it catches its own plant**, because
it once passed clean while silently stripping a real leaked credential URL. That
is the same negative-control discipline every check in this repo carries:

> **A check that has only ever passed is indistinguishable from one that cannot
> fail.**

### What none of this proves

| | |
|---|---|
| **No test asserts the dependency direction.** | Nothing fails if an `@fde/*` package imports an engagement tomorrow. `leak:check` would catch the *vocabulary*, not the *edge*. |
| **`@fde/scanner` has one caller, not three.** | It was extracted to fix a bug class in three copies; only pharma is converted. `leak-check.mjs` and steering's guard still carry their own strippers — the disagreement that motivated the package is not fully closed. |
| **The line counts are `src/` only.** | They exclude tests-in-place, scripts, corpora and generated output, so they measure written surface area rather than everything a package ships. |
| **"Would lift into a customer's repo" is a claim, not a result.** | It has been tested once, by `@fde/bedrock` being written as `@fde/foundry`'s sibling. No package has yet been lifted into an actual second repository. |
